controlsMoving.title: Controls: Moving Around
controlsMoving.description:
[Arrows] or [WASD] move. [Z] confirms and talks. [X] cancels. Hold [Shift] to run.

Running spends [AP]. A full meter lasts about [90 seconds]. Walking refills it slowly, standing still refills it fast. Battle skills use the same meter.

[Z] acts on the tile you face. [Z] on a companion opens their Empathize sheet.

[C] kicks. Kicks break crates, force doors and shove objects. A kickable object makes a sound. A locked door takes [7 to 15 kicks].

controlsMenus.title: Controls: Menu Hotkeys
controlsMenus.description:
[Tab] opens the menu. Each screen also has a letter key, pressed on the map:

- [I] inventory, [C] character, [R] equipment, [P] skills, [J] quests
- [M] minimap, [B] build, [V] vehicles, [F] factions, [H] holdings
- [K] cooking, [L] this book, [N] training, [Y] bestiary, [U] biologics
- [O] options, [G] sandbox (tester builds only)

In the menu: [1] Thinker, [2] multiplayer, [3] Hypernet. On the map, [1] to [9] fire the quick bar.

[WASD], [Z], [X], [Q], [E] and [T] are reserved. [F9] quicksave, [F10] quickload, [F11] fullscreen.

controlsMouse.title: Controls: Mouse
controlsMouse.description:
The mouse does not move your character.

- [drag] pans the camera. It snaps back when you walk
- [wheel] zooms, world map only
- [hover] shows one event's label, [Alt] labels all of them

In battle: [left click] an enemy to use the selected command on it, [right click] cycles commands, [wheel] scrolls, [1] to [5] fire.

controlsGamepad.title: Controls: Controller
controlsGamepad.description:
A controller works in every screen, menus, star map and 3D minigames included.

- [left stick] moves, [right stick] pans
- [R3] labels every event on screen
- [L2] / [R2] zoom the world map, [right stick] scrolls long overlays
- [L1] / [R1] cycle tabs, change character, step the quick bar

Opening a [search field] still needs a mouse.

controlsRemap.title: Controls: Remapping
controlsRemap.description:
[Options] > [Commands]. Keyboard and gamepad remap separately. Every command can be rebound.

Commands added by this game: [Zoom In] (Q, LB), [Zoom Out] (E, RB), [Kick] (C, RT), [Run] (Shift, LT).

controlsScreen.title: What Is On The Screen
controlsScreen.description:
The [party HUD] sits top left: name, level, [HP], [AP] orb, [MP]. The acting member is lit.

[Chips] run beside each card. On the map: hunger, sleep, hygiene, cravings, illness. In battle: stat changes, class resources, states. A chip colours at the [warning] line and again at the [critical] line.

In a vehicle, the vehicle takes a row above the crew, with [fuel] in place of MP.

The [quick bar] sits bottom centre: items on the map, skills in battle.

The HUD can be turned off in [Options] > [Video].

controlsSearch.title: Searching Inside Menus
controlsSearch.description:
Every long list has a search strip, this book included. It starts as a magnifier at the top of the page.

- while typing, [no menu hotkey fires]
- [Escape] empties the field, [Escape] again leaves it

The [main menu search] covers several screens at once: carried items, gear worn by companions, skills, recipes you can make now, bestiary creatures.

savingGame.title: Saving, Autosave and Quicksaves
savingGame.description:
The game [autosaves] on map change, at most once every few minutes, into a normal slot.

[F9] quicksaves and [F10] quickloads, over [3 rotating slots] that any playthrough can overwrite.

Deleting a [permadeath] save keeps its diary.

worldsFolders.title: Worlds and Savegames
worldsFolders.description:
A [world] is a folder, and several can exist at once. Create them on the [Worlds] screen. Until one exists, Explore, Reconnect, Story Mode and Sandbox are greyed out.

A world is generated in full before it is played: [a century of history], people, homes, jobs, shop rotas, the dungeon, politics, factions, epidemics.

Every playthrough in a world starts in the same place, already changed by the ones before it. The clock only moves [forward], so a loaded save resumes from the latest date that world reached.

Other playthroughs appear as [characters on the map], where they were last saved.

optionsMenu.title: Options
optionsMenu.description:
Options is split into tabs:

- [Video]: resolution, fullscreen, pixel perfect scaling, retro shader, UI scaling, party HUD
- [Audio]: volumes, battle music picker
- [Gameplay]: party formation, auto idle explorer, world map hints
- [Commands]: keyboard and gamepad remapping
- [Experimental]: includes the local language model, which can write NPC dialogue instead of the Markov chain

Fullscreen turns itself on the first time a distributed build runs, then keeps your setting.

modsUpdates.title: Mods and Updates
modsUpdates.description:
The game reads a [mods] folder next to the executable. Each subfolder mirrors the game's own folders, so a mod can replace a data file or add content. [Desktop build only].

In the [Mod Manager], [Enter] toggles a mod and [arrows] move it in the load order. The [bottom] of the list wins.

The title screen has an [UPDATES] entry. It downloads only the files that differ from the build's, installs nothing until all of them are checked, backs up what it replaces, and needs the game reopened. There are [2 channels], stable and unstable, and any earlier build can be restored.

partyBasics.title: The Party
partyBasics.description:
[3 members]. The first is the [leader]: the one you steer, the one whose needs drain fastest, the one NPCs answer to.

A [4th companion] walks along without being a member. It never fights and cannot be hurt.

Each member has their own needs, opinions, reputation, specializations and standing with the other two.

[Formation] is set in Options. [Close] walks everyone in the leader's footsteps. [Loose] lets them wander. A loose member with a meter under [35%] goes off to eat, wash, play or rent a room, paid from the party purse.

[Run for 2 seconds] to call everyone in.

partyCreation.title: Making Your Characters
partyCreation.description:
Characters are made one at a time, in [3 ways]:

- [Quick]: look, class, traits, gear
- [Dossiers]: pre-made characters. Some are reusable in any world, the rest are spent once used. A dossier can bring a vehicle, a hometown and alternate skins
- [Detailed]: the whole sheet, down to ideology, morality, orientation and backstory

Starting gear is picked by [price], not power: the cheapest weapon of each type, on a fixed budget per class. Trait gear is granted on top.

partyClasses.title: Classes
partyClasses.description:
A class sets starting stats, the schools you learn fastest and a favoured element.

Each class has a [primary] and a [secondary] category. Primary gives [3x] progression at [half price]. Secondary gives [1.5x] at full price. Anything else needs a skill already known in that school and costs [3x].

Training lists your own curriculum, but outside skills are still learnable.

Any class can equip any weapon. Weapon skill is a [trainable proficiency] instead.

[Creature classes] are a separate set: Feral, Mimic, Monster, Mana Cyborg, Ghost, Zombie, Mutant, Drone. A character on one of them is an animal, not a person.

partyTraits.title: Traits
partyTraits.description:
Traits are bought at creation from a pool of [points]. Positive traits cost points, negative traits give points back.

They change base stats and grant skills, items and gear. They are also read during play: NPC first impressions, how much anyone minds your condition, which specializations start ahead, what companions do in their free time.

Traits are [permanent].

partyAttributes.title: Attributes
partyAttributes.description:
- [STR]: carrying capacity, physical damage
- [CON]: damage absorbed, how long a choke is held
- [DEX]: speed, precision, evasion, escaping holds
- [INT]: learning, mathematical magic
- [WIS]: judgement, resistance, intuitive magic
- [PSI]: luck. Enemy reactions, loot rolls, hidden rolls in your favour

The battle HUD shows each one as a multiplier, for example [STR 1.4x].

partyCreatures.title: Playing A Creature
partyCreatures.description:
A party member can be a [creature], built from one archetype or two crossed.

The archetype sets the body: that species' exact parts, reach, hands and weak points.

A [creature class] is non sentient and holds no job, money, creed or property. A [civilised class] is a person shaped like an animal, treated as a person everywhere.

Anatomy decides how many weapons can be held, whether you can be choked, and what a pregnancy produces.

partyPortraits.title: Portraits and 3D Models
partyPortraits.description:
Each character is drawn one of [3 ways], chosen at creation and never mixed:

- [bust]: a hand drawn portrait
- [model]: a body built limb by limb. Each limb can take the matching part of any creature, with sliders for height, build, ears, nose and skin
- [sprite]: used by monsters, recruited enemies and summons

The status screen, the dialogue portraits and the Empathize panel all use this choice.

partyRecruiting.title: Recruiting People
partyRecruiting.description:
[3 ways] in: talk a monster round in battle, ask a townsperson through [Empathize] once they think well enough of whoever is asking, or adopt a creature and train it.

A recruited townsperson leaves the map for good. Their profile, personality, traits, skills, wealth, history and standing move into the party actor.

The party holds [3], so someone must leave for someone to join. Retired members go back to the [dossier board].

partyPets.title: Pets, Followers and Children
partyPets.description:
A [4th companion] follows the party without being a member. It never fights, cannot die and cannot be targeted.

A [follower] comes from a monster that talks, a [pet] from a monster that does not, a [child] from a pregnancy.

Only one walks with you at a time. The [Followers] page swaps and releases them.

Pets and followers can be [trained] into party members, into the classes their species allows. Training is measured in world clock minutes and shortened by [Animal Training] or [Leadership]. Only the companion currently with you makes progress. Children and summons are never trained.

partyReproduction.title: Reproduction and Pregnancy
partyReproduction.description:
Every body has a [reproductive type], set at creation from the species:

- [Testicles]: fertility, count, motility and morphology follow hormones and condition
- [Uterus]: a [28 day] cycle, fertile on days [12 to 16]
- [Oviparous]: a clutch of [1 to 4 eggs]
- [Plant]: seeds develop endlessly and stockpile until planted
- [Mitosis]: the body divides and makes a copy

A pregnancy runs the term of the species. [Biologics] shows gestational age and fetal stage. Symptoms arrive as states.

Newborns appear in [Followers] as children with the parent's face. Mitosis makes a copy, not a child.

partyDeath.title: Death, Gravestones and Permadeath
partyDeath.description:
Falling in battle is not automatic death. [Health protection] and [danger warnings] let you break off, and fleeing always works.

A dead character leaves a [gravestone] where they fell. It stays on the map and is where restoration is performed.

Under [permadeath] the character is gone for good, and their quicksaves with them. A wiped party ends that party only. The next one starts in the same world.

Healing does not put lost limbs back.

partyBanterPage.title: What Your Companions Say
partyBanterPage.description:
Two or more companions hold discussions of [2 to 4 lines], drawn from what is happening: a recent purchase, low health, a meter under [35%], a diary line from the last few hours, the biome, the road, the money, the leader, the plan.

A third member's [personality] usually closes the exchange.

They also talk while driving, and on trains, coaches and taxis.

partyAutoIdle.title: The Auto Explorer
partyAutoIdle.description: An [Options] toggle lets the game play itself while you are idle. The party explores and looks after its needs on its own, paying the same costs you would. Control returns the moment you press anything.

progressLevels.title: Levels and Experience
progressLevels.description:
Experience comes from [winning fights]. A level raises the six attributes and the HP and MP pools.

Levels are a small part of power. Skills, specializations, gear and the condition of the body matter more.

progressKnowledge.title: Knowledge Points
progressKnowledge.description:
[Knowledge points] buy skills. KP belongs to the [party], not to one member. They come from fights scaled against the party's median level, and from quests, adventures, dreams and Raman scans.

Prices come from combat value: MP and AP cost, damage scaling, repeats, targets hit, states inflicted. The weakest skill is [50 KP], an ordinary one a few hundred, the strongest a couple of thousand. [Esoteric] costs [10x] its score, [Forbidden] costs [100x].

[Primary] school halves the price, [secondary] pays full, outside schools pay [3x].

progressAtlas.title: The Atlas of Circles
progressAtlas.description:
Skills are laid out as a [sphere grid]. Each school is a circle: rings from its weakest working outward to its strongest, with upgrade spurs on the rim ending in esoteric workings.

You can only buy a skill [adjacent to one you know]. The [innermost ring] of every school is always open.

[Forbidden] workings sit in the centre, connected to nothing. The whole school must be known before any of them opens.

One school is shown at a time: use the pager or walk off the rim. [Wheel] and [Shift] zoom, [drag] pans.

progressTraining.title: Training and Progression
progressTraining.description: Each member trains [1 skill at a time]. Winning a battle is worth [3 points], using a skill of the same category is worth [2]. [Primary] categories multiply this by [3], [secondary] by [1.5].

progressSpecializations.title: Specializations
progressSpecializations.description:
About [800 specializations], from Wrestling to Accounting to Beekeeping. Each is governed by one attribute and has [5 tiers], Untrained to Master.

A level is the highest of [3 sources]: trained through play, granted by class, granted by a trait.

They train by doing. Cooking raises cooking, selling raises haggling. The [leader] earns full value, anyone else present earns [35%].

They are read everywhere: forging quality, lockpicking, hold damage, what a merchant accepts, whether a recipe can be read at all.

progressPassives.title: Class Passives
progressPassives.description:
Every class has [signature passives]. They need no slot and no activation. Some work in combat, some only outside it.

They are listed on the status sheet under [Passives].

progressLoadout.title: The Nine Skill Slots
progressLoadout.description:
A character carries [9 skills] into a fight, out of everything they know. The skill menu is tabbed by role, and the 9 chosen fill the [battle quick bar].

Changing the loadout between fights is [free].

progressFusion.title: Fusing Spells
progressFusion.description:
On the [Magic] page, two abilities can be forged into one.

- the [dominant] slot takes a spell you know and sets damage, scope, hit type and icon
- the [recessive] slot takes a spell or a skill. A skill makes the result a skill

The fusion costs the [sum] of its parts in MP and AP, and the sum of their teaching prices in KP. The components are [forgotten] on fusing, and the fusion can be split back into them at any time.

progressGrimoires.title: Grimoires and Skill Books
progressGrimoires.description:
A [grimoire] offers [5 random workings] and lets one reader take one. The 5 are rolled once when the book is opened, against the whole party. Switching reader does [not] reroll them.

A reader can only take an offer whose [MP cost] fits their maximum MP and that they do not already know. The party's median [PSI] raises the chance of a [Forbidden] working appearing.

There are school specific grimoires, category specific skill books, and the [Forbidden Grimoire], which offers nothing else.

progressBladeSeeds.title: Blade Seeds
progressBladeSeeds.description:
[12 seeds], one per weapon type. A seed upgrades a whole [weapon type], not one weapon.

It grows as that type is used, and what it grows into is [procedural]. A seed outlasts the weapon that carried it.

gearSlots.title: Equipment: Hands and Slots
gearSlots.description:
There is no dual wield flag. Weapon slots come from [anatomy]: every body part the species can hold a weapon with is a slot. Hands take a weapon or a shield, so two shields are as legal as two swords.

- a [two handed] weapon needs two free hands
- a body with no hands holds its weapon in the [mouth], and anything fits. Samurai keep a mouth slot on top of their hands
- [8 slots] maximum, however many limbs a body has
- past [2 weapons] each parameter becomes the [median] of what is carried, and 2 random weapons swing each turn
- losing a limb removes its slot and drops what it held

gearProficiency.title: Weapon Proficiency
gearProficiency.description:
Any class can equip any weapon type. Skill with a weapon is a specialization, one per type, [12 in all]. It starts at [Intermediate] for the types your class was once limited to and [Untrained] for the rest.

It scales the weapon's parameters: [33%] Untrained, [67%] Beginner, [100%] Intermediate, [110%] Advanced, [125%] Master.

Winning a battle grants [1 point] per equipped weapon type.

gearScaling.title: What a Weapon Scales On
gearScaling.description:
A weapon does not always scale on STR. Its [attack skill] sets the attribute it reads, and the equip screen names it when the slot is selected.

With no attack skill it reads [STR]. Otherwise [DEX], [INT], [WIS], [CON], [PSI], or a mix of two.

gearArmor.title: Armour and Derived Stats
gearArmor.description:
Equipment feeds [4 out of combat stats] besides defence: [Substance], [Stealth], [Arcane], [Intimidation].

- clothes: Substance and Stealth
- robes: Arcane
- light armour: Stealth
- heavy armour: Intimidation
- daggers and bows: Stealth
- swords, heavy weapons, axes and claws: Intimidation
- staves: Arcane
- whips, projectiles and guns: Substance

They decide how people answer you, what a guard assumes, and which approaches are open.

gearModifiers.title: Modifiers on Gear
gearModifiers.description:
A weapon or armour piece can carry [1 modifier], which changes its stats, price and traits.

- [Sharp]: raises STR and price on weapons
- [Refined]: raises CON, WIS and price on anything
- [Poisoned]: adds poison to a weapon
- [Worn]: lowers CON, WIS and price on armour

The modifier moves with the item.

gearWeight.title: Weight and Encumbrance
gearWeight.description: Every item has a [weight] and the party has a [carry capacity]. Going over it raises a notification that stays up until you are back under.

gearBackpack.title: The Backpack
gearBackpack.description:
The backpack is tabbed by category, with the weight readout, the detail card and the favourites bar.

[9 favourite slots] hold usable items and share the quick bar with battle skills. On the map, [1] to [9] use that slot. In the backpack, the same keys assign the inspected item. Items can be [dragged] onto slots, [right click] clears one.

Only [usable] items can be favourited.

gearArtifacts.title: Artifacts
gearArtifacts.description:
[Artifacts] are generated items, weapons and armour, each named and unique.

The [Artifact Analyzer] on the Hypernet reads what an unfamiliar one does.

gearContainers.title: Containers and Storage
gearContainers.description:
Chests, cupboards, crates and sacks store items and can be emptied or filled at will.

The [extradimensional container] and the holds of the camper and the car travel with the party.

gearRarity.title: Loot and Rarity
gearRarity.description:
Random loot is scaled against the party's [median level], not the leader's.

Items print in their [rarity colour] everywhere: reward popup, backpack, shop counter.

Item descriptions are combinatorial and resolved from the [world seed], so the same sword reads the same way all through one world and differently in the next.

needsOverview.title: The Five Needs
needsOverview.description:
Everyone in the world carries [5 meters]: [Hunger], [Sleep], [Hygiene], [Company], [Fun].

All five run [100 to 0] and drain with time. Time passes as you walk: [1 minute per 10 steps], [10 minutes per world map tile], [2] in a vehicle. The [leader] drains fastest, and running drains everything faster.

They show as chips beside each party card, colouring below [20%] and again at [0].

At [0]: hunger drains HP, sleep drains MP, the rest cost you socially and mentally.

[Augments] can slow a need, stop it or reverse it: a ruminant stomach burns less, a somnologic regulator never tires, a self cleaning dermis gains hygiene as you walk.

needsHunger.title: Hunger and Nutrition
needsHunger.description:
Every edible item carries [calories], [fat] and [protein], and eating credits all three. A meal is worth what it contains, not what it costs.

Hunger can pass 100, up to [150%]. Above [110%] you are [Overfed], a state with penalties. Above [100] it burns [3x] faster.

Cold burns calories for warmth and heat raises metabolism, so both ends cost food.

At [0] you take continuous HP damage until you eat.

needsSleep.title: Sleep, Rest and Time Awake
needsSleep.description:
[2 separate values] are tracked.

The [sleep meter] is how tired you feel. Coffee or a sit down refills it. At [0] it drains MP.

[Time since you last slept] only clears with a night's rest: zero up to a day awake, climbing through two, maxed at a [week]. It turns dreams hostile and pulls the party's mind apart.

Beds, campfires, tents and world map camps open the [rest menu]. [Wait] and the [T] hotkey only move the clock.

[Cryogenic sleep] is separate: pick a year to wake in and the world moves on without you.

needsHygiene.title: Hygiene, and What It Costs You
needsHygiene.description:
Hygiene drains slightly faster than sleep. Refill it at a washroom, shower, sink or fountain. Loose companions go and find one below [35%].

It works both ways: your hygiene is read against the person you talk to, and theirs against you. At [60%] and above nobody notices. Below that, each point costs a little under [half a point of standing], capped at [45].

[Traits] set how much it matters. [Feral] ignores it. [Ascetic] barely notices. Street Urchin, Cave Dweller, Survivalist, Farmer and Veteran mind little. Proud, Wealthy, Beautiful, Perfectionist, Noble, Hypochondriac and Germaphobe mind a lot. Several such traits multiply. One "does not notice" trait overrides them all.

[Courting] reads both bodies again at a heavier weight, and names which of the two needs a bath.

needsSocial.title: Company
needsSocial.description:
Company is refilled by [talking], to townspeople or between two of your own.

A [loose] member short of company walks up to someone and starts a conversation. That conversation moves what the other person thinks of them, and hygiene counts in it.

Gaining [standing] with someone feeds the social meter of whoever gained it.

needsLeisure.title: Fun
needsLeisure.description: Fun is refilled by [playing]: arcade cabinets, pianos, pool tables, card games, and jokes that land in conversation. A joke that lands also raises the listener's Fun for the [rest of the day].

needsAddiction.title: Cravings and Withdrawal
needsAddiction.description:
[5 traits] are dependencies: [alcohol], [caffeine], [nicotine], [narcotics], [gambling]. Only a member with one has a craving meter.

The meter runs [backwards]: [0] is satisfied, [100] is withdrawal. It climbs while unfed, and feeding it drops it to 0. [Withdrawal] only lifts once the craving is well below full, so one dose does not clear it.

Cravings climb slower during sleep.

bodyParts.title: Limbs and Organs
bodyParts.description:
Every character and monster has individual [limbs and organs], each with its own health, taken from its species.

Damage spreads across parts. A part at [0] is [destroyed]: it carries a permanent penalty and changes what the body can do. A lost hand takes its weapon slot. A body with no hands holds a weapon in its mouth. Damaged legs cost movement and evasion. A part at 0, damaged or severed can neither grapple nor be grappled.

[Vital organs] are shielded from ordinary damage and only opened by [targeting].

Parts [never heal on their own]. They are treated at a clinic, restored by magic, or replaced with a prosthetic. In [Blood and Oil] a slashing blow can take a part off the body, augment and all.

The status sheet shows the body part by part under [Anatomy].

bodyBiologics.title: Biologics
bodyBiologics.description:
[Biologics] is the deep readout: vital signs, hormones, blood chemistry, brain regions and their activity, blood type, reproductive cycle, and every condition acting on the body.

[Heart rate] follows what is happening to you. [Hormones] follow sleep, injury and pregnancy. [Blood type] never changes.

The [Ley Vein] system links this page to limb damage: blockages show up here when the body has been hurt.

healthDiseases.title: Diseases
healthDiseases.description:
Each disease has a [transmission chance], one or more [vectors] (airborne, saliva, bite, contact, sexual and others), stat modifiers while carried, and often a state that only appears after the carrier has walked a set number of steps. That delay is the [window period].

Transmission is rolled between your own members each time you open the [pause menu], and between the party and a townsperson each time you open their [Empathize] panel. [Venereal] diseases never spread by proximity.

Every NPC carries a [medical history], readable on the Health tab of their panel.

[Diagnose] examines the whole party and names every illness carried, window period included.

healthEpidemics.title: Epidemics
healthEpidemics.description:
A [continental epidemic model] runs above individual illness. Each infected town has its own curve, resolved at [midnight], and exports cases along map distance with occasional long jumps. [Public response] builds the longer a town has been infected, and eventually breaks the wave.

An [outbreak] is a pathogen with a case fatality ratio. A [hysteria] has none: dancing fever, genital theft panics, phantom gassers. A hysteria is caught by [witnessing] it and spread by [talking] about it.

Every world starts with [3] running: one hysteria, one ordinary outbreak, one rare and mortal.

Anyone in an infected town is exposed. Outbreaks move mood, hiring, shop traffic, need drain, gossip and the news. The [Eurodemics] observatory tracks all of it.

healthSurgery.title: Clinics, Prosthetics and Field Surgery
healthSurgery.description:
A [clinic] can install a body part, remove one, replace one or fit an implant. Installing costs [1000 euros] per percent of body health the part represents, removal [100]. [Vital parts cannot be removed].

[Field surgery] is the same operation on the road: pick a patient and a surgeon, fit only parts already carried, take an augment out but never seat one, and pay [nothing].

Every operation is a [roll], with the odds shown first. The surgeon's [Surgery] specialization gives [35 / 50 / 65 / 78 / 90 percent] by tier. Then: a roof [+10], a cave [-5], the open [-10], rain [-15], a storm [-25], snow [+5], operating on yourself [-15].

A failure wounds the patient elsewhere. Vital organs are only at risk in [Blood and Oil].

healthAugments.title: Augments
healthAugments.description:
The [Augments] register has 2 lists. [Fitted] is every augment the party wears, with its wearer and socket. [Catalogue] is everything that exists, readable before paying for the graft.

The dossier gives the cost, the bonus, the skill it teaches, and every socket that accepts it, creature sockets included.

The right augment also slows a [need], stops it, or reverses it.

healthWeatherBody.title: Weather, Temperature and the Body
healthWeatherBody.description:
[Ambient temperature] is shown on the travel card. Cold burns calories for warmth, heat raises metabolism, so [hunger drains faster at both ends].

Weather also costs [field surgery]: rain [-15], storms [-25], snow [+5].

combatBasics.title: How a Fight Starts
combatBasics.description:
There are [no random encounters]. Every monster stands on the map with its [level] over its head, and you fight it by walking into it.

Turns are [individual]: each battler acts on its own turn, in [agility order], and your action resolves the moment you choose it.

Enemies [keep their damage between fights]. A wounded monster you ran from is still wounded when you come back, and corpses stay on the map.

[Fleeing always works].

combatCommands.title: The Battle Commands
combatCommands.description:
Besides [Attack], [Guard], [Skills], [Magic], [Item], [Escape] and [Reload], the menu has 4 commands of its own:

- [Check]: opens the enemy's body, limb by limb, with the chance of hitting each
- [Target]: aims your next blow at one part
- [Wrestle]: takes hold of the enemy
- [Talk]: another way to end a fight

Wrestle and Talk take no loadout slot and cannot be forgotten. They come from the body, not the class.

Mouse: [left click] an enemy to run the selected command on it, [right click] cycles, [1] to [5] fire.

combatAP.title: MP and AP
combatAP.description:
[MP] is magic: spells cost it, it refills slowly, and most rites and summons are held with it.

[AP] is momentum, capped at [100]. Battle skills and sprinting on the map spend the same meter. Running empties it in about [90 seconds], walking refills it slowly, standing still fast.

Cost follows type: [magic] is written in CamelCase and costs MP, a [skill] is written in plain words and costs AP.

combatBodyParts.title: Hitting What You Aim At
combatBodyParts.description:
Monsters have the same limbs and organs the party does. [Check] lists every part with its condition and the chance to hit it. [Target] aims your next blow at one.

The chance comes from the part's [size], your [weapon type] read against your stats, and a random swing of [10%] either way.

Destroying a limb removes what it does: a broken leg slows, a ruined wing stops flight, no hands means no weapon held. [Vital organs] can only be reached by a targeted attack.

A finishing blow can [sever] the part.

combatDamageTypes.title: Damage Types & Piercing Mechanics
combatDamageTypes.description:
Every attack, skill and weapon carries a [damage type]: [Explosive], [Piercing], [Cutting], [Blunt], [Area], [Abstract], [None].

Explosive, Piercing and Cutting can [sever] a part on a lethal blow. The rest ruin it in place. [Area] and [Explosive] spread over [2 to 4 parts], everything else hits only the part aimed at.

[Piercing] also ignores most defences:

- through [Guard] for half damage
- hits a [Protect] substitute in full and carries through to the ally behind for half
- ignores [Divine Shield] completely
- passes through [Magic Reflection] and hits the target directly

combatWrestle.title: Wrestling
combatWrestle.description:
[Wrestle] is open to any body with one limb whole enough to grip. It costs nothing and is never learned.

It replaces the command menu with the [grapple plan]: which of your limbs takes the hold, which of theirs, and which hold. Each row shows the odds. A part at 0, damaged or severed can neither grab nor be grabbed.

- [Grapple], STR vs DEX: takes hold. Everything else needs one first
- [Strike], STR vs DEX: needs no hold, can concuss on the head
- [Joint lock], DEX vs STR: pins, often breaks the guard
- [Wrench], STR vs CON: heavy damage, can cause bleeding
- [Slam], CON vs DEX: guard broken, winded, chance to stun
- [Choke], CON vs CON, head only: guard broken, vitals exposed
- [Rip], STR vs CON: low odds, enormous damage, can tear the limb off

Everything scales with the [Wrestling] specialization. A trained [martial art] adds its own finishers for free.

combatTalk.title: Talking to Monsters
combatTalk.description:
A monster able to understand you can be talked to. [Talk] opens a panel with the odds of each approach beside it.

Every enemy has a [disposition] from [1 to 100], rolled when it appears and shifted by species. Hurting it costs [5 to 15 points].

- [Chat] builds rapport. Chance is disposition plus a fifth of the gap between your PSI and its own, floor [10%], cap [95%]
- [Surrender], same odds. It leaves the fight
- [Join the party] needs a free slot, and above [80] disposition uses the chat chance
- [Follow you], or be adopted as a pet. A talker needs [70] disposition
- [Insult] always lands and lowers disposition
- [Throw a stone], or [pet it]

Creatures counted as forces rather than people, [petrodemons] above all, refuse every approach.

combatEnemyLevels.title: Enemy Levels and Where They Live
combatEnemyLevels.description:
The [Enemy Spawn] option sets how enemy levels are chosen.

- [Balanced]: a band above the party's median. Median L meets [L to L + 7 + L/10]. One encounter per world tile sits above the band as a boss, never over [100]
- [Distance from spawn] (default): level by how far the world square lies from the one you started on. [Level 1] at home, the top of the roster at the far corner. Each square fields creatures whose habitat matches the biome
- [Chaos]: the whole roster flat random, [1 to 110], redealt on every map entry

No creature is exclusive to a country. Every nation holds every creature its biomes hold and only changes how common each is.

The [calendar] sits above all three. In [2001] the band is as the mode sets it. From [2002 to 2009] it climbs [10 levels a year]. [2010] and [2011] have no band. From [2012] nothing below [level 80] roams, and there is no ceiling.

combatMovementAI.title: How Monsters Behave
combatMovementAI.description:
Each roaming monster has a [movement personality]: what it does while idle, how it notices you (sight range, facing cone, line of sight) and what it does once it has.

Fixed, Random, Approach, Fleeing, Skittish, Grazer, Sentry, Guard, Patrol, Territorial, Ambusher, Lurker, Mimic, Swooper, Stalker, Hunter, Charger, Pack, Erratic, Drifter, Orbiter, Scavenger, Coward.

A [Grazer] never notices you. A [Sentry] has a cone and can be walked around. An [Ambusher] is not where it appears to be. A [Pack] does not fight alone.

combatSafety.title: Danger Warnings and Surviving a Blow
combatSafety.description:
Before a fight the party's [median level] is compared with the enemy, and a [warning] appears when it is out of range.

In a fight each character has [1 health protection charge]: the first blow that would kill them leaves them at [1 HP]. It comes back next battle. [Blood and Oil] removes it.

combatModes.title: Difficulty and Combat Modes
combatModes.description:
Several settings change what combat is. Most are chosen at character creation.

- [Peaceful]: monsters act only once hurt, per enemy. An unprovoked one skips its turn, roaming monsters wander instead of chasing, and a wipe respawns you with nobody dead
- [Ordinary]: death leaves a gravestone and the run continues
- [Hardcore] and [Blood and Oil]: death is a game over and the character is removed. Blood and Oil also drops the health protection charge and lets a slashing blow take a part off the body
- [Card combat]: replaces the command menu
- [Map battle]: fights on the live map

combatMapBattle.title: Map Battle Mode
combatMapBattle.description:
An experimental option fights every battle on the [map you are standing on].

Everyone fights from where they stand. Any monster that wanders within a few tiles [joins in] with its own HP card and turn. A townsperson near the brawl joins [your side] if the party is well liked or if they are brave, fighting from their own level, stats and skills.

[Move] repositions the acting battler at a range driven by agility. Weapons have [reach]: [1] melee, [2] for spears, whips, staves and flails, more for bows, guns and thrown weapons, [line of sight] required. Water means swimming, which costs more movement.

Round order: party and enemies interleaved by agility, then townspeople, then the [world step], where every roaming monster, townsperson and your pet move one tile at once.

combatSummons.title: Summons
combatSummons.description:
A [summon] is a temporary 4th member. It lives for [that battle only]: never saved, never in the menu, gone when the fight ends or when you stop paying for it.

What answers: a creature, a person the party has marked, the pet on your leash, a reflection of the summoner, or a revenant of a traveller you lost.

Numbers are re-cut against your median and the troop on the field, then multiplied by the rite's share: a [familiar] is half a traveller, a [titan] slightly more than one. A bruiser stays a bruiser. The [elder entity] arrives with its own numbers and drains the summoner in about [3 turns].

[Upkeep] by kind:

- [HP]: demons, undead, shadows, swarms, titans
- [MP]: elementals, celestials, fae, the void
- [AP]: the reflection
- [euros]: constructs, war machines, dragons, champions
- [soul]: spirits
- [oil]: the petrodemon
- [a fixed few turns]: beasts, verdants, familiars, called people

When you cannot pay, it leaves. A summoner who cannot pay in blood is left at [1 HP].

The [familiar] belongs to one character. Their class decides which creature answers, so changing class remakes the pact.

While a summon is out, a [hyper bar] fills with damage the party deals. Full, the summon fires its [ultimate], which grows with the party's median level in brackets of [10].

A summon is computer controlled and has [no 1 HP protection].

Outside a fight the same rites work and what they call walks in a trailing slot, each point of MP buying a fixed number of steps.

combatArena.title: The Arena
combatArena.description:
The arena has [2 shapes]: a [gauntlet], a run of fights in a chosen level bracket, and a [biome trial], a run against the fauna of a chosen biome.

The party is [rescaled] to the bracket, and a random roster can be fielded instead of your own.

Wins build a [streak], which pays ascending money and items.

combatBulletHell.title: Bullet Hell Sequences
combatBulletHell.description:
Some fights break into a [bullet hell] sequence: you steer a small craft, dodge the enemy's pattern and shoot back.

Damage taken and dealt there counts in the fight.

combatSpirits.title: Spirit Battlers
combatSpirits.description:
Defeated enemies join a [spirit roster]. One can be fielded in place of an ordinary battler, at a cost that scales with what it was.

The feature runs on its own [switch].

combatMimic.title: Mimicry
combatMimic.description:
[6 mimic skills] copy other bodies:

- [Partial mimicry]: the enemy's face and map sprite, numbers unchanged
- [Full mimicry]: stats, HP, MP, AP, skills, body and looks
- [Mirror]: re-uses the enemy's last skill against it
- [Copy ally]: a companion's name, class, skills, sprite and body
- [Random]: full mimicry of a creature drawn at random
- [Mutation]: merges 2 random archetypes into your own body parts

All six need [exactly one enemy] on the field. Copying a body copies its limbs, which changes what you can hold and where you can be hurt.

combatThrow.title: Throwing Things
combatThrow.description:
Items, weapons and armour can be thrown up to [8 tiles], diagonals included, with flight simulated from the item's [weight]. Heavy things travel a short way.

A thrown item stays where it lands.

combatCorpses.title: Corpses, Rewards and Cooldowns
combatCorpses.description:
The [reward popup] names everything at once: items in their rarity colours, money, experience and [knowledge], the last scaled by enemy level against the party median.

The dead leave [corpses] on the map. Enemy events are removed or put behind a [cooldown] rather than respawning at once.

Every creature met is written into the [Bestiary].

elementsOverview.title: Elements: How They Work
elementsOverview.description:
[9 damage types]: Physical, Fire, Ice, Thunder, Water, Petro, Wind, Sacred, Cursed.

Every creature answers each one with a [rate]. Above [100%] is a weakness, below is resistance, [0%] is immunity, and a [negative] rate absorbs the element and heals from it.

The battle HUD prints what you have discovered about the enemy in front of you, and the [Bestiary] keeps it.

States interact: [Wet] raises lightning damage, [Oily] raises fire damage, [Static] absorbs lightning.

elementPhysical.title: Element: Physical
elementPhysical.description:
Edges, points, weight and fists. Most weapons deal it and most armour is built to stop it.

It [severs limbs], breaks guards and lands holds. [Heavy armour] resists it and feeds Intimidation, [light armour] trades that for Stealth.

Spirits, oozes and gases resist it.

elementFire.title: Element: Fire
elementFire.description:
Applies [Burned], which keeps dealing damage after the blow.

Raised against anything [oily], dry or wooden. Resisted by the [wet] and the cold blooded. Absorbed by things that live in fire.

elementIce.title: Element: Ice
elementIce.description:
Applies [Cold], and [Freeze] at strength, which stops a body acting.

Raised against [wet] targets. Used on a burning target it removes the burn.

elementThunder.title: Element: Thunder
elementThunder.description:
Applies [Static], and [Paralysis] at strength.

Devastating against a [wet] target. Absorbed by anything already [Static], which heals it instead.

Machines and constructs usually resist it.

elementWater.title: Element: Water
elementWater.description:
Applies [Wet], which raises lightning damage, lowers fire damage and is read by several states.

Its own damage is [low].

petro.title: Element: Petro
petro.description:
Oil and what comes out of the ground with it.

Petro belongs to the [petrodemons], which refuse every approach and drop [barrels] rather than coins. [Oil] works as a currency: it prices the post between worlds, it holds the petrodemon summon on the field, and the market trades it.

Petro damage leaves the target [flammable].

elementWind.title: Element: Wind
elementWind.description:
Air, pressure and cutting motion. It [unbalances] and displaces.

Flying creatures deal it and resist it. It is weakest against [rooted] or heavy targets.

elementSacred.title: Element: Sacred
elementSacred.description:
Answered badly by the [undead] and the [cursed]. It [heals] a target on the right side of the line.

Sacred workings usually carry protection and purging alongside damage.

elementCursed.title: Element: Cursed
elementCursed.description:
Rot, ruin and draining. Dealt by the undead, answered by the sacred.

Cursed workings often cost more than MP, and the strongest are tagged [Forbidden], which puts them at the centre of their circle at [100x] their value.

Efficient against the living. It [heals the already dead].

worldMapPage.title: The World Map
worldMapPage.description:
The world map is one map of Europe, each tile a whole region. Walking one costs [10 minutes] of game time, [2] in a vehicle.

[M] cycles the display: hidden, corner minimap, fullscreen. In fullscreen, [drag] pans and [wheel] or [Q] / [E] zoom.

Stepping onto a tile offers to [keep going] or to [visit the square], which builds its local map. [T] switches between the world map and the last local map.

Loose companions keep a [2 tile] leash up there. Squares marked [???] are adventures.

worldProcedural.title: Procedural Maps
worldProcedural.description:
Almost every map is [generated]. A world map square becomes a map when you enter it, built from the [world seed] and its [coordinates], so it is the same map every time you return.

The [biome] sets the tileset and what grows there. [Roads] run straight, cross, turn and loop back mid-map when they lead nowhere. [Rivers] are wide and irregular, fixed to one width at the borders so they continue into the next square, and only reach a border if the square beyond is water. [Coastlines] are sampled along the border so neighbours draw one continuous shore. On top go hand authored [32x32 prefabs] and terrain features scattered by biome.

Walking off the edge loads the [neighbouring square].

worldBiomes.title: Biomes
worldBiomes.description:
The [biome] of a square sets its tileset, terrain features, fauna, music, weather and forageables.

Some are [special variants], rolled rather than fixed: spirit woods, crystal fields. Certain creatures live only there, and a special biome always places [at least one] of them, whatever the spawn mode or the calendar.

[Roofed] biomes (cellars, temple interiors, cave dens, dungeons) are entered through a structure entrance.

worldStructures.title: Structures Under the Map
worldStructures.description:
Entrances on procedural maps are [walked into], not pressed. What lies behind is rolled from the world seed, the square and the tile, so one stairway always leads to the same place.

- [stairs down]: any structure. Cellar, dungeon, crypt, catacombs, mine, cistern, warren, oubliette, library, forge, bunker, laboratory, shrine, tunnel, grotto, lava tube, barrow, station, salt works, cave den, temple
- [stairs up]: things built above ground and since buried
- [cave]: dens, frozen caves, crystal caves, fungal caves, lava tubes, sea grottoes
- [grate]: a sewer, only in towns that declare one underneath
- [hatch]: a patron's vault, full of money and rare weapons

The surface limits the options: ice fields hold frozen caves, a graveyard holds catacombs.

worldHouses.title: Houses, Inns and Shops
worldHouses.description:
[Doors] on procedural maps open onto generated buildings. Houses, inns, shops and tower blocks are seeded by [coordinates], so a door is always the same business.

Buildings can have [several floors]. Shops and inns wear their name over the door.

The [lock] is checked before the door animation runs.

worldTerrain.title: Working the Terrain
worldTerrain.description:
Face a terrain feature and press the action button to work it.

- [trees]: felled with an [axe] in the inventory
- [rocks]: mined with a [war pick], any heavy weapon or a [chipped pickaxe]
- [plants]: picked with nothing at all
- anything else can be [dismantled]

The payout is [crafting materials]. Mining sometimes yields an [ingot].

Foraging always pays [plant matter], and about [2 picks in 5] also pay something edible. What turns up depends on the country: acorns and chanterelles in a forest, cloudberries on tundra, dates in a desert, samphire on a marsh, blind mushrooms underground. Training [Foraging] raises the odds.

[Alien] surfaces forage nothing. Food there comes from butchering local wildlife.

Felled trees and worked features [stay gone] when the map is rebuilt.

worldDungeon.title: The Dungeon and the Tower
worldDungeon.description:
One great dungeon, its layout rolled when the world is created.

Above ground it runs in [10 levels], [A to J], each of [9 ordinary floors] and [1 elevator floor]. The elevator and the floor list jump to any floor already reached. Unseen floors show as [???].

Below ground is the [lower tower]: [92 generated floors], each one of the structures from the procedural catalogue. Stairs read the other way down there: [deeper is a smaller number].

worldPuzzles.title: Puzzles
worldPuzzles.description:
Maps carry puzzles:

- [sokoban blocks], pits that swallow them, goal tiles, reset and undo shrines
- [pressure plates], timed plates that must be held, levers, gates wired with [and / or] logic
- [ice floors], arrow tiles, conveyors
- [crystal switches] that flip sets of blocks between solid and open
- [torches] to light, sometimes timed, sometimes spreading fire
- [colour tiles], lights out grids, coloured doors, combination locks
- [warp pads], crackable walls, light beams to redirect, clones that copy your moves, magnetic objects, counterweights, floodable rooms

worldFog.title: Fog of War
worldFog.description:
Some maps are covered in [fog], pushed back by walking. Vision is a [cone]: you see where you face, and turning is how you look around.

Uncovered ground is [remembered] per map.

worldDigging.title: Digging and Secret Doors
worldDigging.description:
Some walls can be [broken through], turning a dead end into a route. [Digging] is the deliberate version.

[Secret doors] look like wall until interacted with, then stay open.

Locked doors give [3 options]. [Peek] teleports you for a look without letting you move. The menu that follows holds the other two: [pick], a falling block minigame that needs [lockpicks], or [break in], which is filed as a [crime].

worldMovement.title: Water, Climbing and Bridges
worldMovement.description:
Face water and press the action button for the [water menu]: [swim], which disables sprinting, [fish], with a rod in the party, or [dive].

[Climbable] terrain is climbed slowly, facing up. Height is tracked, and jumping down from [3 tiles] or more costs [5% health per tile] fallen.

[Bridges] are layered. Enter from the approach and you walk on the bridge. Enter from anywhere else and you pass under it, for the whole span.

worldWeather.title: Weather, Time and Seasons
worldWeather.description:
The clock starts at [8 AM on 1 January 2001] and never stops. Time advances as you walk and jumps when you sleep, wait or travel.

[Weather] is generated per country, seeded on the date, and changes on entering an outdoor map. The country sets sunrise and sunset, seasonal temperatures, and which weather is possible.

Rain applies [Wet], storms apply [Static], snow applies [Hot].

The screen is tinted by time of day and temperature: [blue] for cold, [red] for hot.

worldDreams.title: Dreams
worldDreams.description:
Sleeping can drop you into a [dream], rolled from a seed. It deals [4 to 7 regions] and mixes them: backrooms, offices, escher stairs, drowned places, cosmic voids, megastructures, car parks, hospitals, cathedrals, factories, carnivals, sewers, fleshpits, gardens, ruins.

- [WASD] walks, the [mouse] looks, [space] jumps. Hold jump while standing still to [take off]
- the [action button] uses the weapon in your right hand. The [wheel] steps through every weapon in the game
- touching anything alive moves you to [another dream], and so does walking head on into a wall
- holes have [no floor], and falling far enough leaves the dream

Every dream has [1 to 3 laws]: the ground breathes, gravity is light or crushing, colours invert, figures move only while unwatched, time hitches, your size changes, the dream repeats itself.

There is [no end] to it. The ground loops in every direction and stacks upward as long as anyone climbs.

Every minute inside rolls a chance of [knowledge], reported when you wake.

worldAdventures.title: Adventures on the Map
worldAdventures.description:
Some world map squares carry a [???] marker, redrawn once a day. Stand on it and [Investigate] plays a branching adventure written for that place.

The last node pays out: a relic, gear, salvage, money, a fight with something native, a minigame, an augment, a change of faction standing, a crime filed against you, a rest, or nothing.

The [leader] goes in. Some choices are only offered to a leader of a particular [temperament].

A biome carries [1 marker], [2] if it is very large, and a named place carries its own on top. An answered square [stays answered].

worldBologna.title: Bologna
worldBologna.description:
Bologna is in the game as itself, rasterised from OpenStreetMap into a grid of large cells that join [seamlessly] at the borders.

Every building has a door on its [south face] and every door is a way in. Most are homes, the rest shops and inns seeded per tile.

The city is populated at runtime: townspeople from the world's own faces and from Bolognesi born there, plus wildlife by habitat, street animals on pavements, waterfowl and fish in the canals, birds on rooftops.

worldPlatformer.title: Platformer Maps
worldPlatformer.description:
On a map tagged as a [platform] stage the controls become a side scroller: [left] and [right] walk, [space] jumps, [shift] runs, and jumping against a wall [kicks off] it.

Ladders are climbed with [up]. Companions follow your exact path a moment behind.

worldFlying.title: Flying
worldFlying.description:
Flight moves you like an [airship]: any direction, over everything. [Confirm] lands you.

It comes from particular items, skills and vehicles.

worldConnections.title: The Map of Maps
worldConnections.description:
A second map shows every map you know and how they connect, built from the transfer events and doors between them.

Click a node to set it as [destination] and the shortest path lights up. A [compass] in the corner points at the next waypoint.

worldTreasure.title: Chests and Treasure Rooms
worldTreasure.description:
Chest contents are generated against the party's [median level]. An emptied chest [stays empty].

Some maps hide [treasure rooms]: reachable, randomly placed rooms with heavier contents.

worldTechTree.title: Research and Discovery
worldTechTree.description:
[8 trees] of discovery: Social Sciences, Alchemistry, Technomagica, Physics, Arcane, Mathematics, Astronomy, Theotecnical.

The scientific trees follow real progress from [2001 to 2012]. [Arcane] and [Technomagica] follow the rediscovery of lost magic and its fusion with machinery. [Theotecnical] follows the Vatican rebuilding its dogma around engines. Each also has fringe branches and a few nodes from the [world seed].

Completed nodes record the [leader] who got there first. Researching one consumes [crafting materials] and returns most of that cost as [refined byproducts].

travelOverview.title: Fast Travel
travelOverview.description:
Any place marked as a destination can be travelled to. [Bus stops] and [signposts] open the travel screen.

A destination and a mode put you on a [travel map] for that transport, with a [countdown] that keeps running while you open menus or fight. At zero you arrive.

travelModes.title: The Thirty Ways to Travel
travelModes.description:
Each destination lists the transports that reach it. There are [30], trading money against time.

- [Walking] is free and slowest. A [bicycle] is cheap and slightly quicker, a [horse] better. [Car sharing] and the [camper] cost fuel instead of money
- [Bus], [train], [taxi], [boat] and [ferry] are the ordinary fares. The train is fast for its price, the taxi the same speed for twice as much
- [Flights], [limousines], [helicopters] and [private jets] are expensive. A private jet runs [10x] walking speed. [Cruises], [submarines], [balloons] and [zeppelins] are slow and dear
- Exotic: [magic carpets], [dragons], [teleport circles] at [20x] walking speed, [hypermetro], [maglev], [hyperloop], [starships], [wormholes], [quantum jumps], [time machines] and [dimensional crossings]. A dimensional crossing costs [1000x] the base fare and is [1000x] as fast

Cost is the [base fare times distance]. Speed divides the time.

vehiclesOverview.title: Owning a Vehicle
vehiclesOverview.description:
A vehicle is proven by an [item]. Holding the key, the deed or the broom puts it in the [Vehicles] menu.

Vehicles are [parked in the world], not carried. Each one's position is stored, world square and underground layer included.

Walking up to one opens its menu: [drive], [enter the interior], [storage], [refuel], [repair].

vehicleCamper.title: Vehicle: The Camper
vehicleCamper.description:
The largest vehicle. [100 litres] of fuel, a walk in interior with beds and storage, refuels at any roadside pump.

A [ground] vehicle, so it crosses road tiles faster than open country. Fast travel by camper costs [fuel], not money.

[2 workshop modules] extend it. [Aquatic] floats and dives, with [C] to dive and surface. [Flight] fits rotors, with [F] to take off and land.

It is driven directly, not by fast travel.

vehicleCar.title: Vehicle: The Car
vehicleCar.description:
Faster than the camper and much smaller. [60 litres] of fuel, a small interior, refuels at any pump, takes the road bonus. Fast travel by car costs [fuel], not money.

Any parked car can be [stolen]: face it, press the action button and choose to steal. That opens the [lockpicking minigame] and needs a [lockpick], or a [skeleton key], which opens it outright. Failure files a [vehicle theft] against you.

vehicleBike.title: Vehicle: The Bike
vehicleBike.description: Human powered, so it needs [no fuel]. The fastest vehicle available early, takes the road bonus, and costs nothing to keep.

vehicleBroom.title: Vehicle: The Flying Broom
vehicleBroom.description:
Needs [no fuel], works indoors, and stows into your pack as an item.

It [flies] over every tile of every map: walls, water, cliffs and events. It lands on anything that can be stood on, rooftops and bridges included.

It takes [no road bonus].

vehicleBoat.title: Vehicle: The Boat
vehicleBoat.description:
An inflatable dinghy. It carries no fuel and travels only on [open water]. There is nothing to repair and nowhere to store anything.

The party is drawn aboard, everyone on the benches, with the pet in the stern.

vehicleStarship.title: Vehicle: The Starship
vehicleStarship.description:
[200 litres] of fuel and a full walk in interior. It [cannot] be refuelled at a roadside pump.

Hull, layout and appearance are generated from a set of [trait axes] and can be edited.

It needs [no driver]. It is used from the [star map].

vehicleFuel.title: Fuel
vehicleFuel.description:
The [camper], the [car] and the [starship] burn fuel. The bike, the broom and the boat do not.

Fuel is bought at [pumps] at a price that moves with the world's [oil market]. The starship cannot use a roadside pump.

Consumption is by [distance] and differs per vehicle, with a gauge in the corner while driving. Running dry [strands you].

vehicleRepair.title: Vehicle Damage and Repair
vehicleRepair.description:
A vehicle has [12 parts], each with its own health.

- [Critical], they stop it dead when broken: engine, transmission, brakes, steering
- [Performance] only: battery, alternator, radiator, fuel system, exhaust, suspension, tyres, body

Damage comes from what you hit. Something soft marks the front only. Another vehicle at road speed is felt throughout.

Repairs consume [crafting materials]. While riding, the vehicle's condition shows as an [HP bar] on the party HUD.

vehicleUpgrades.title: The Workshop
vehicleUpgrades.description:
Vehicles are upgraded with [crafting materials] at the [workshop].

[4 upgrades], [3 levels] each: acceleration, speed, fuel capacity, structural health.

[2 one off modules], camper only: [aquatic] and [flight].

[Aerodynamic] work reduces how much game time a world map tile costs.

Each level costs more exotic materials, from steel and plastic through titanium and circuitry to varlenian matter, nanotubes and quantum components.

vehicleCrew.title: The Crew
vehicleCrew.description:
The [leader] takes the wheel when a journey starts, and only the [driver] earns the vehicle's specialization experience.

Time at the wheel is tracked as [strain]. [Alertness] is the sleep meter less strain. Below [40%] the wheel passes to the best rested member above that line, and everyone not driving sheds strain. When nobody is fit to relieve the driver, they keep going and you are told.

[Passengers] nap below [40%] sleep, until full or the end of the journey. A [crash] wakes them and keeps them awake for an hour.

The bike and the broom have no rota. The starship's crew tends one need at a time out of the hold.

vehicleDriving.title: Driving in 3D
vehicleDriving.description:
The camper is driven directly across the world map: the same biomes, the same roads, the same distances.

[3 views], swapped with [Tab] or [Y]: first person at the wheel, chase camera with zoom, and a free roam cabin view.

[W] throttles, [Shift] is turbo, [S] brakes and reverses, [A] and [D] steer, [space] is the handbrake, the [mouse] looks.

It has a [5 speed automatic], lateral slip so the handbrake drifts, grip that differs between asphalt, dirt, grass, sand, snow and rock, and gravity on slopes.

[Traffic] runs [9 vehicle types], hatchback to city bus. They brake, take junctions and can be crashed into.

On foot the leader's [weapon] is in hand, and the [d-pad] steps through the weapons they can hold.

roadTraffic.title: Traffic, Roadkill and Theft
roadTraffic.description:
A car occupies as many tiles as its sprite is long: it never clips a wall it passes, cars collide bodywork against bodywork, and anyone under the bodywork is [run over]. Only a [moving] car hits anything. Town traffic brakes for people, highway traffic does not.

Being hit knocks you clear and triggers an [accident]. An NPC hit by a car takes [injury conditions] written onto their profile. A creature hit hard enough dies.

Driving over someone injures them, drops their opinion of [every] party member, and files a [hit and run]. Ramming a creature flings it off the bonnet the first [2 times]. From the [3rd] the odds it turns and fights climb steeply.

A car that pulls over and lets its driver out sits [parked and stealable] until they return.

peopleOverview.title: People Are Real Here
peopleOverview.description:
Every person on the map has a full [profile], generated from their name and the [world seed]:

- a [personality] out of [25 archetypes], which sets how they speak
- [traits], the same ones your characters carry
- an [ideology] on [5 axes]: economy, authority, tradition, militarism, mysticism
- wealth, skills, inventory and equipment
- a faction, a home, a job and a schedule
- a [backstory] from your world's history
- a [medical history], past diseases and badly healed bones included

Part of the population is [animals], from the same system. A creature on a beast class is [non sentient]: it holds none of that, and answers in its class voice.

peopleEmpathize.title: The Empathize Panel
peopleEmpathize.description:
Talking to someone properly opens the [Empathize] panel: identity, history, biology, health, romantic life, daily life, politics, and a log of their last conversations.

From it you can [talk], [praise], [insult], [joke], [give], [trade], [court], [propose] and [recruit], and read why they feel as they do about you.

[Standings are per party member], and only the member doing the talking moves theirs.

A [free chat] field takes typed input and generates a reply. With the [local language model] enabled it writes the reply, otherwise a Markov chain does.

peopleOpinion.title: How Somebody Decides What They Think of You
peopleOpinion.description:
An NPC's opinion of one of your characters is built from [4 parts]:

- [base opinion], moved by everything you have done to them
- [trait compatibility], applied before a word is spoken
- [ideology], how close your creeds sit on the 5 axes, worth up to [12 points] either way
- [hygiene], read on both of you

[Attraction] is tracked apart from opinion. Conversation, gifts and trade move opinion only. [Courting] moves attraction, and reads trait compatibility and hygiene again at a heavier weight.

peopleLives.title: People Have Lives
peopleLives.description:
Everyone's life advances whenever time does, minute by minute and through any skip.

- they are born somewhere on a date and keep a record of every [move] since, with reasons
- they meet, date, marry, divorce and separate, preferring partners from their own settlement
- they hold [careers] from the real job list, with a history from their first working year, changes as they age, and retirement
- dishonest ones carry [convictions], sentences served off screen and outstanding bounties. A conviction can cost someone their job

A year in [cryogenic sleep] is a year in which everyone aged, changed jobs, married and buried each other.

peopleTalking.title: What People Say to Each Other
peopleTalking.description:
Two people who wander close together stop and hold a [conversation], one line at a time in thought bubbles. The [tone] (positive, negative, neutral or debate) comes from what they think of each other and from their personalities. Finishing one [moves both opinions].

People sharing a room while busy trade [2 line] exchanges without stopping.

Each of the [25 personalities] has its own lines for weather and time of day, its own inner monologue, and its own openers and closers.

The last [20 conversations] of every person can be read in their panel.

peopleSettlements.title: Settlements and What Happens To Them
peopleSettlements.description:
Every settlement has [3 civic meters]:

- [Prosperity]: employment, the national economy, recent events
- [Security]: crime per head, the honesty of the local captain of the guard, national stability, how wanted you are
- [Mood]: the other two plus unrest, festivals, epidemics and street traffic

[Episodes] sit on top of them:

- [crime wave]: starts when security collapses. Crime pays better and the crackdown catches more thieves, so the wave breaks itself
- [boom] and [bust]: start at the extremes of prosperity and swing hiring, crime, divorce, shop prices and market sentiment
- [festival]: declared by a thriving town. Mood and bustle up, shops fuller, pickpockets in the crowds
- [epidemic]: rare, and worse in miserable towns. Mood, hiring and shop traffic collapse until it burns out

Unemployment feeds crime, crime feeds crackdowns, crackdowns feed prisons, prisons feed unemployment. All of it reaches the news, the stock market, hiring and gossip.

peoplePolitics.title: Politics
peoplePolitics.description:
Every hyperpower has a [government]: theocracies, single party states, parliamentary monarchies, technocracies, sultanates, divine pantheons, serene republics, corporatocracies, warband confederacies. Each has parties, orders or clans, a political class with [charisma], [integrity], [cunning] and [ambition], a head of state, and meters for [legitimacy], [stability], [unrest], [economy] and [treasury].

[Elections] run in each power's own idiom: general elections, papal conclaves over several ballots, politburo plenums announcing 99% results, wealth weighted shareholder meetings, goblin moots where the runner up risks being eaten, divine ascension tournaments, palace successions, and the Archive's Great Examination.

Between elections: scandals, edicts, protests, riots, coups, revolutions, assassinations, referendums, and rulers ageing and dying.

Every person has a [political identity]: 5 axis ideology, a party, an engagement level from apathetic to organizer, a voting record, and grudges against the parties that beat theirs.

Each settlement elects a [mayor] every year, who appoints a captain of the guard, a tax collector and a high priest.

peopleFactions.title: Factions and Reputation
peopleFactions.description:
[18 factions]. Standing with each runs from [-100 to +100], moved by contracts taken, crimes committed, adventures resolved and sides taken.

A faction attached to a [hyperpower] is a branch of it, so credit earned with the parent can carry its branches.

Standing decides what work is offered, what prices are quoted, who will speak to you, and which seats you may take.

peopleONU.title: The Assembly
peopleONU.description:
Every hyperpower holds a seat inside the [Omega Tower]. Once a [game week] the delegations argue about alliances, trade, war and recent events.

A party member can [take a seat]. The seat, the standing and the weekly [stipend] are that character's alone, and the stipend scales with their standing with the power they serve. Let it fall far enough and they are [dismissed]. Only powers that already think neutrally or well of them will take them, a character joins [once], and resigning costs far more than joining paid.

A session rolls [1 to 3 motions]. [2 to 5 delegations] take the floor, you answer, and every seat votes. Ballots are [public], each tile turning green or red as it is read, or [secret], shuffled so only the tally is certain.

[Grave motions] (war, admission, territory, artifacts, theonuclear devices and the goblin question) go to the [Security Council]: the [5 strongest powers] of your century. Majority carries and the [Secretary General] breaks a tie. Without one, the motion fails.

The [Tourists] hold a chair with no ballot and admit nobody.

lawCrime.title: Crime and Bounty
lawCrime.description:
Every crime is filed by name with its own [bounty value], and your bounty is the sum of them. Theft, breaking and entering and vehicle theft are deliberate. Running someone over is not.

Bounty lowers the [security] meter of settlements you are in, becomes gossip, changes how the guard behaves, and is read out in court.

The record is settled through the [police portal].

lawPolice.title: The Police Portal
lawPolice.description:
The [N€police] application on the Hypernet settles your record without waiting for you to be caught.

- [case file]: every charge with its fine, settled one at a time or all at once
- [self-report]: confess something not yet registered, at [half] the usual fine
- [custody]: turn yourself in, or request a hearing before Eris

Both custody options leave the computer: the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

lawTrial.title: The Trial
lawTrial.description:
Justice is administered by [Eris], and a trial is [generated], not scripted. The courtroom, gallery and staff are rolled fresh each time, and she cites invented case law mid hearing.

[Counsel] is retained before the hearing: hire one of [5 advocates], nominate a party member, or stand alone. The five are people from your world, fixed for its lifetime, and recruiting one strikes them off the bar.

The brief shows each option's level, INT, WIS, [Law] level, opinion of you, fee, and the projected odds of every outcome. The odds swing on [Eris's mood], and in some moods she throws counsel out, which loses their bonus and does [not] refund the fee.

Defending yourself, or having a companion stand up, earns a few points of the [Law] specialization per hearing. A professional teaches the party nothing.

The hearing is a [plea], then [choices], then a [verdict] that depends heavily on her mood. Evenings spent with Eris raise a [bond]: a warmer mood wheel, a lower conviction chance and shorter sentences.

[Sandbox] mode has a reverse trial, where you play Eris.

lawPrison.title: Sentences and Prison
lawPrison.description:
Sentences come in [2 shapes].

- a [named term] is served by the game clock: time passes in the cells and the bounty is cleared on release
- an [open ended] sentence has no release date and grinds the bounty down day by day

Turning yourself in at the police portal goes straight to the second kind, with [no hearing].

lawEris.title: Dating Eris
lawEris.description:
Eris can be [courted]. An evening with her is a generated scene.

It happens in a [biome], and each biome has its own opening, questions, romantic beat, chaotic beat, shared activity and local incidents. A [scenario] is rolled on top (picnic, seance, stakeout and others), so one biome hosts many evenings.

Her [mood] is rolled from [16]: playful, romantic, chaotic, nervous, confident, caring, guilty, crazed, psyched out, high on solipsism, eldritch, melancholy, smug, paranoid, prophetic, bored. It can shift mid date. In the [eldritch] mood her lines warp, her pulse reads things that are not numbers, and the portrait misbehaves.

Each date also rolls a [register] (sincere, capricious or completely bonkers), which scales how often the evening is interrupted and how hard her feelings swing. She interrupts with [dares], up to robbing a bank.

[2 heartbeats] are drawn on screen, yours and hers. She keeps a [separate score for every party member], and sometimes turns towards one of your companions mid date.

The first date that ends well pays a [blade seed], once per save.

societyMail.title: The Post
societyMail.description:
A party can write to another party in the [same world], or to a party in a [different world] on your machine. The letter waits in their mailbox until someone plays them.

A letter carries a [delivery date] on the recipient world's clock, and the sender can hold it back by days, months or years.

[Money] and [goods] can be enclosed. They leave the sender's pockets at once and are handed over when the recipient collects them.

Post inside one world is [free]. Crossing to another is priced on the two commodities that survive the crossing, [oil] and [souls]: their prices multiplied, doubled once per step of dimensional distance, never less than [300,000 euros].

societyNews.title: The News
societyNews.description:
The world writes its own [news], and items carry effects: property prices, shop occupancy, market sentiment.

Settlement episodes, riots, coups, elections, epidemics and the mayor's divorce all become headlines.

societyDiary.title: The Party Diary
societyDiary.description:
The [diary] is the record one party keeps of its own life, written as it happens.

It takes in journeys, first entry into a named place, dungeon floors, sleep, fights, bosses, arena streaks, people joining and leaving, deaths, levels, pets, births, friendships, courtships, evenings with Eris, diseases, limbs lost, augments, surgery, notable finds, trade, thefts, property, loans, crimes, trials, prison, shifts worked, crops, crafting, skills, research, quests, bestiary entries, minigames, television and dreams.

[Not recorded]: ordinary conversation, statue descriptions, states coming and going, discarded items.

Entries are stored as [keys], so a diary written in one language reads correctly in another. The [banter] system turns the newest lines into what the party talks about.

societyTopics.title: Conversation Topics
societyTopics.description:
Some dialogue teaches a [topic], written in square brackets in the line where it appears. Once one character hears it, [the whole party knows it].

A dialogue option that requires a topic is [invisible] until then, not greyed out.

The [Topics] tab of this book lists them with who knows each one.

societyArmy.title: Armies
societyArmy.description:
Troops are recruited by faction, up to [100], and the count is drawn over your sprite on the world map.

Other armies fill the world map. About [a fifth] are faction armies of [200 to 1000] troops, which stay inside their own country's borders. The rest are independent bands of [5 to 30], which roam anywhere and spawn near you.

Touching one starts a [field battle] in a real time tactical view: your units in [yellow], theirs in [red], formed up by role, close quarters in front, support behind, ranged at the back. Wounded troops drop to [1 hit point] and stop. Killed troops are [gone for good].

societyMultiplayer.title: Multiplayer
societyMultiplayer.description:
[2 ways] to play with other people.

[Online], through a central server or through Steam. A server session supports many players, of whom the nearest [8] are drawn on one map. A Steam lobby caps at [8] and sets rich presence, so friends see [Join Game] in their list.

[Local split screen], 2 players on one machine with a gamepad each. The viewports merge into one when the players are close, and player two interacts with events directly.

Split screen also runs a [hot seat] for minigames. Real time arcade carts let either player steer, chess, pool and bowling alternate turns.

During a [map battle] player two drives the second party member.

societyHistory.title: The Century Behind You
societyHistory.description:
Every world is generated with a century behind it: an alternate history of Europe from [1900 to 2001].

It produces coups, elections, purges and assassinations; wars, sieges, mutinies and conquests; [50 kinds] of paranormal anomaly, occult rites and the Squishing itself; scientific expeditions, natural disasters and organised crime. The weighting favours the paranormal and the occult.

That history sets which [hyperpowers] exist and how strong they are, which [5] sit on the Security Council, what epidemics the last century saw, and what the people you meet lived through.

The full timeline is in the [Historical Archive].

econMoney.title: Money
econMoney.description:
Money is [euros], written with 2 decimal places. The only other currency is the [arcade token].

The [Assets] screen adds cash, bank balance, property, shares and livestock, subtracts debts, and calls the result [net worth].

econShops.title: Shops
econShops.description:
Shops come in several kinds.

- [counter shop]: a grid of goods with categories, sorted by price
- [delivery order]: arrives in [1 to 7 days] depending on price, up to [6] at once
- [random daily shop]: stock seeded from its coordinates and the world seed, rerolled every in game day
- [vending machine]: the same, in a [4x4 grid] of coded products, [3 purchases] per slot per day, with at least one odd item each
- [teaching shop]: sells skills instead of goods, at a discount

[Tax] is charged on everything except skills, at a rate that moves with the economy and never drops below [30%]. A shop cleaned out restocks at [midnight].

econStealing.title: Stealing
econStealing.description:
Anything on a shop's shelves can be [stolen]. The steal window lists what each shop holds, with a [success percentage] per item from your [agility], the item's [value] and its [weight]: light and cheap is easy, heavy and precious is not.

Ordinary shops are scanned across the whole map. A random daily merchant only within [5 tiles].

Getting caught files a [crime] and lowers the settlement's [security]. During a [crime wave], stealing is measurably harder.

econBank.title: Banking and Loans
econBank.description:
The bank takes [deposits], pays [interest] on the balance, and [lends] against a due date. Both run on the world clock, so they accrue while you walk, sleep, travel or sit in cryogenic sleep.

Missing the [due date] is penalised.

econStocks.title: The Stock Market
econStocks.description:
The market trades [2 commodities], [oil] and [soul crystals], from a single page terminal. Prices are a [random walk] tilted by what happens in the world: settlement booms and busts, news events, the state of the powers.

The [oil price] is also what the fuel pump charges and what a letter to another dimension costs.

econProperty.title: Real Estate
econProperty.description:
[30 properties] across the towns, rated [1 to 5 stars]. A 1 star place costs under [1000 euros]. 4 and 5 star places are estates.

Buy one outright and you can offer it for [rent] to NPCs, collected at [midnight] and on the [first of the month]. Rent it as a [tenant] and it is a monthly cost, with no subletting. Missed payments [evict] you.

Prices move with news events tied to specific towns.

An [inn room] is separate: booked for [24 game hours], and it cannot be double booked.

econShopOwning.title: Owning a Shop
econShopOwning.description:
A shop you own holds [stock], a [warehouse] and a [production line]. Items with recipes can be produced from materials on the premises, deliveries are made at delivery points on the maps, and [NPC staff] can be hired to do the work.

[4 pages]: overview, shelf stock, warehouse, and the catalogue of what can be produced.

econWork.title: Work
econWork.description:
More than [30 jobs], and any party member can be sent to work.

Each job states its [stat requirements] first. A member short of them is flagged but never blocked.

A [shift] takes game time, and the outcome comes from the worker's stats and luck. A [disaster] can cost money, deal damage, or leave a status effect.

The [Job Offers] menu lists what is available now and where.

econQuests.title: Quests
econQuests.description:
Quests are [generated], and a board's offers come from where it stands.

Every quest is a list of [steps]: a simple quest has [1], a chain [2 or 3]:

- reach a set of world coordinates, or a named destination
- open an auto placed chest, or [dig] a site, which needs a shovel
- land on a planet and open its sample cache
