- kill a specific high level enemy, spawned at a tile, which [stays there until killed] even if the quest fails
- scan statues or signposts, or dismantle a number of trees, rocks or piles of rubble
- open the quest board of another town, or interview a citizen through [Empathize]
- hand over items, or wait for goods to arrive
- win arena fights, defeat a number of enemies, or hold a number of oil shares

[Terms] are shown before you accept: reward, upfront cost, advance paid, deadline, failure penalty, breach bounty and reputation change. [Scams lie about them].

Rewards and difficulty scale on the party's [median level]. The second tab lists signed contracts with progress and countdowns.

The [quest log] is a board of sticky notes in [3 columns].

econNotices.title: Reading a Notice
econNotices.description:
A quest notice is written in the [voice] of whoever pinned it up: a corporate contract, a goblin scrawl, a redacted military bill, a nervous private plea. Dozens of [faction registers] and a couple of dozen [personality registers] exist.

What is left out, what is over explained and what is plainly a lie are readable before you accept. The [terms] panel gives the numbers.

econVending.title: Arcade Tokens
econVending.description: Arcade machines take [tokens]. Tokens are bought with euros at the [converter machine] or at the [Token Exchange] on the Hypernet, and unused tokens can be cashed back in at the [same rate].

craftThinker.title: The Workbench
craftThinker.description:
The [Thinker] is the general workbench: [assembling] and [dismantling]. The recipe is written on the item itself.

A recipe stays [hidden] until it has been made once, though common ones are on the board from the start.

Base materials come from dismantling the world: felling trees, mining rocks, breaking furniture, salvaging gear.

craftForge.title: The Forge
craftForge.description:
Every weapon and armour in the game is on the [forge] board from your first visit. Training changes which of them you can [make].

[4 tabs]: what you can smith now, what you lack materials for, what is above your training, and what this party has already forged.

About [31 trades] are in play, one per item: a robe is [Tailoring], a wig is [Wig Making], a rifle is [Gunsmithing], a circuit woven coat is [Electronics].

Each finished piece has its own identity, so two never stack. [3 things] set its sheet: how far past the required tier the smith's trade is trained, how rich the bill was, and the [heat] on the day. Every parameter then drifts on its own and the price follows.

A [finish] is picked before forging and stays on the piece.

[Smelt] melts a carried piece back into materials: [half] the bill, more from a well made piece.

The party switcher decides which tab an entry falls into and who earns the specialization points.

craftAlchemy.title: Alchemistry
craftAlchemy.description:
Every alchemical recipe is readable from the start, and none is gated behind a class.

A recipe is copied onto a [bench], and the bench is what you edit and run, so one recipe can be set up two ways at once.

Success is a [skill check]. Meeting every requirement is [0% failure]. Each tier short raises the chance. Tiers [above] what the recipe asks pay out as extra product, up to a cap.

Step durations are [game minutes], so a batch cooks while you walk, work, travel or sleep.

A bench set to [repeat] rebuys its reagents, and stops when the pack cannot pay for a run.

craftCooking.title: Cooking
craftCooking.description:
Cooking combines [2 recovery items] into one. The first item's recovery is [doubled] and the second's is added, so [order matters].

Cooking two of the same thing adds a random [adjective] instead, with a bonus or a penalty. The name is built from the first word of the first ingredient and the last word of the second.

craftBrewing.title: Brewing
craftBrewing.description:
Barrels ferment on the [world clock]. Load a barrel and leave it: brewing and distilling proceed while you play.

The slowest crafting, and it needs [no attention].

craftFurniture.title: Building and Furniture
craftFurniture.description:
The [Build] menu places furniture on tiles, snapped to the grid. Pieces can be crafted from materials, bought, and [dismantled] to recover them. Some can be flipped.

[Wall] furniture goes on walls only. The upper tiles of ordinary furniture may overlap a wall, the lower tiles may not.

The Build menu is also where [animals] are bought.

craftPlants.title: Farming
craftPlants.description:
Any [tilled soil] can be farmed. Plants follow the clock, the [season] and the [weather].

They grow only in their own seasons, and are [dormant] outside them. Rain speeds growth by [30%], storms by [10%], snow [halves] it, and a [greenhouse] runs at full speed all year. A plant at [100%] is harvested on the spot.

Tilled soil on procedural maps is farmable too. The first visit to a world square rolls which patches are already sown and with what, so a whole field grows the same crop.

craftAnimals.title: Animals
craftAnimals.description:
Animals are bought in the [Build] menu and placed on a tile, then managed from the [Assets] screen as livestock to collect from, sell, or turn into a pet.

They grow from [baby to adult] over a set number of days, and adults [produce] at intervals: an egg, a pail of milk, a fleece.

Every animal pays [company] into the party's social need when you interact with it, [once per game day]. Dogs, donkeys and roosters produce nothing and are kept for this.

craftApiary.title: Beekeeping
craftApiary.description:
A hive is a [colony simulation]. Queen, workers, nurses, guards, foragers and drones each run from egg through larva and pupa to adult and death. The colony produces [honey], [pollen], [royal jelly] and [wax].

Seasons and weather act on it, [disease] and [pests] threaten it, and its mood and efficiency follow how it is kept.

craftArtifacts.title: Procedural Artifacts
craftArtifacts.description:
[Artifacts] are generated items, weapons and armour with rolled properties. They appear in loot, in vaults, at the end of adventures, and from certain rites.

One rite turns a [party member] into a weapon.

craftLoot.title: How Loot Is Rolled
craftLoot.description:
Random loot is scored from [0 to 100]: the party's [median level] plus a [difficulty modifier] carried by the place. The score picks the [rarity band], from almost everything common at [0 to 20], through a balanced spread at [50], to almost everything legendary at [100].

Rarity is read off [price], and the same ladder colours item names everywhere.

A [patron's vault] pushes the tables toward the expensive end.

craftContainers.title: Containers
craftContainers.description:
Containers hold items [without limit], and each is unique to its map and event. Contents are generated from the [categories] the container declares, weighted by rarity.

The [extradimensional container] opens from anywhere and travels with the party, as do the holds of the camper and the car.

galaxyOverview.title: The Star Map
galaxyOverview.description:
The star map covers several [scales]: the system you are in, the galaxy, the local group, the supercluster, the cosmic web and the observable universe. At system scale [1 unit = 1 astronomical unit].

[Drag] orbits, [wheel] zooms. Clicking a body offers what you can do: [travel] there, or [land].

Each planet keeps its own day and night, so the hour you land at depends on where you land.

galaxyTravel.title: Travelling Between Stars
galaxyTravel.description:
Select a system and [travel] to it. The journey burns [fuel], and fuel sets your [range].

Only an [ordinary fusing star] can power a refuel. Main sequence stars of every class work, remnants and black holes do not. [Refuel] starts the pumps if you are parked at one, plots a short hop if there is one elsewhere in the system, and otherwise plots a course to the nearest system that has one.

On any map inside the ship the [windows] show where you actually are.

galaxyShip.title: Your Starship
galaxyShip.description:
The ship's hull and layout are [generated] from your [world's seed].

From the [vehicle menu] you can reroll the whole thing or step through individual traits and keep the rest.

Under way the [crew] tends one need at a time: a meal, a wash, a conversation, a game, a shift of sleep. Eating consumes food from the hold.

galaxyLanding.title: Landing
galaxyLanding.description:
In orbit you can [land]. Where landing sites exist you pick from a list, otherwise you touch down on the surface.

An alien surface is an explorable map with dozens of [alien biomes] chosen by the type of world.

- encounters are [not scaled] to your party or your distance from home. The [planet's own level] decides, readable from its [biosignature] before you commit
- there is [nothing to forage]. Food comes from butchering local wildlife
- a body stripped of its resources [stays stripped]

Identified species go into the bestiary's [alien] page.

galaxyAnomalies.title: Anomalies
galaxyAnomalies.description:
Every star system with planets has at least one [anomalous world], marked with a [?].

Holding orbit over it offers to [investigate], [once only]. What follows is a branching encounter written for that kind of world, paying out in a relic, in salvage, in a fight with something native, or in nothing.

galaxyBodies.title: What Is Out There
galaxyBodies.description:
[Stars] come in the real classes and in a couple of dozen exotic kinds: remnants, brown dwarfs, feeding X-ray binaries. Systems can be binary or hold several stars, each travelled to individually.

[Black holes] come in [3 weights] and cannot refuel you. [Rogue planets] drift between the stars with no sun.

About [20 real nebulae] sit at their real galactic coordinates: the Horsehead, the Orion Nebula, the dark nebulae. [Dyson spheres] exist.

Above the galaxy the map continues: local group, superclusters, cosmic web filaments and the shells of the observable universe.

Our own [solar system] is hand authored, with [12 real bodies], its belts and a shell of orbital debris.

galaxyPatrons.title: Patron Worlds
galaxyPatrons.description:
Some worlds in other galaxies are named after the people who paid for the game. They are habitable, they orbit exotic objects, they sit in [9 planet systems] where no two planets share a type, and the star map lists them under [Patrons].

Each of those people also owns a [hatch] on exactly one world map square. It cannot be dismantled and nothing grows over it. Going down opens their [vault]: a great hall with strongrooms and a deep back chamber, with the loot tables weighted to the expensive end.

Hatch locations are [encrypted] in the game data.

galaxySky.title: The Night Sky
galaxySky.description:
A [night sky chart], separate from the star map. Stars are sized by [magnitude] and the constellations are traced over them.

[Tab] switches between [2 constellation sets], European and Chinese, which trace different figures over the same stars.

hypernetOS.title: The Hypernet Desktop
hypernetOS.description:
A simulated operating system of the period: desktop, taskbar, start menu, resizable windows and a set of applications.

Its [file system] and [registry] are saved inside your savegame, so written files and changed settings persist.

- [WASD] or [arrows] move the focus ring, [Tab] cycles
- [Enter] activates, [Escape] leaves a text field, then closes the window, then exits
- on a controller: [d-pad] navigates, [A] activates, [B] closes, the [left stick] is a free cursor

hypernetBrowser.title: App: Hypernet Explorer
hypernetBrowser.description:
The browser: tabs with their own history, an address bar with autocomplete, an explorer bar with search, favorites and history, find on page, view source, downloads, print preview, zoom, a pop up blocker, mail and news, and a [404] page that suggests alternatives.

Every page in the archive is a full document. Preferences, favorites, history and downloads live in the [registry].

hypernetMyComputer.title: App: My Computer
hypernetMyComputer.description:
The file explorer, over the [virtual file system]: drives, folders, My Documents, and everything you or an application has written.

Files open in whichever application owns them: a text file in [Notepad], a saved web page in the [browser].

hypernetNotepad.title: App: Notepad
hypernetNotepad.description: A plain text editor writing into the [virtual file system]. Notes typed here are saved in your savegame and readable by any application that reads files.

hypernetControlPanel.title: App: Control Panel
hypernetControlPanel.description:
Machine settings. Your party's statistics read as [hardware specifications]. Wallpapers and display settings are set here.

Changes are kept in your savegame.

hypernetTVGuide.title: App: TV Guide
hypernetTVGuide.description:
The television listings, read from the broadcast database: every channel, its cast and its programmes.

Selecting a programme plays its broadcast [inline], a line every couple of seconds.

The schedule regenerates every [in game week] and is fixed for that week.

hypernetObjectIndex.title: App: The Object Index
hypernetObjectIndex.description:
A catalogue of every object known to exist: about [1100 dossiers], one per item.

The [left page] is the catalogue, grouped by category. The [right page] is the dossier: identification, lore paragraph, commerce, physical properties, provisioning values, composition and raw declaration tags.

The lore paragraph is combinatorial and resolved from the [world seed]. [Randomize] rerolls it for this window only.

hypernetNeuroPolice.title: App: N€police
hypernetNeuroPolice.description:
The continental police portal, for settling your criminal record without waiting to be caught.

- [case file]: every charge with its fine, settled one at a time or all at once
- [self-report]: confess something not yet registered, at [half] the usual fine
- [custody]: turn yourself in, or request a hearing before Eris

The custody options close the computer: the cells and the courtroom are places on the map.

hypernetEurodemics.title: App: Eurodemics
hypernetEurodemics.description:
The public terminal of the continental epidemic observatory.

- [situation]: outbreaks running, people ill, people dead, towns affected, and a readout of where you are standing
- [outbreaks]: every outbreak burning, each with its daily curve, redrawn at [midnight], over the town by town table
- [archive]: outbreaks this world has closed, plus the epidemics and mass hysterias of the last century

hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.title: App: Artifact Analyzer
hypernetArtifactAnalyzer.description: Analyses [procedural artifacts] and reports what they actually do.

hypernetTokenExchange.title: App: Token Exchange
hypernetTokenExchange.description: Converts [euros] into [arcade tokens] and back, at the same rate as the physical converter machine.

hypernetPhone.title: The Hexphone
hypernetPhone.description:
The party carries a mobile phone: [credit], [contacts], [call history], an [inbox] and a couple of built in [games].

Calling a contact triggers what that person does when called. Incoming calls arrive with an answer or decline prompt.

[Keypad digits] dial and act as shortcuts, [Enter] selects and calls, [Escape] ends and goes back.

[Payphones] share the same contacts and credit but only place outgoing calls.

hypernetTV.title: Television
hypernetTV.description:
Tuning a television to a channel puts you in that channel's [studio], where the cast performs the broadcast: named cast turn to face you and read their lines. A programme with no cast is narrated.

Dialogue splices in the [live state of your world], so the history channel and the news desk read back the simulated century and the current news.

The weekly schedule regenerates every [in game week]. The script is rerolled on every tune in, [10 to 16 exchanges] per slot.

[Commercial breaks] sell a product at its real price, or a political position paid for by one of the powers.

Finishing a transmission raises the whole party's [Fun]. The [Technophobe] trait loses the same amount instead.

hypernetRadio.title: The Radio
hypernetRadio.description:
Radios tune across [AM], [FM] and [EM] bands. The stations are built from the music files the game ships with, so every track is somewhere on the dial.

[Left] and [right] change frequency, [up] and [down] change band, [page up] and [page down] scan, [Enter] marks a favourite.

The last station tuned is [remembered].

hypernetMusic.title: Music and Sound
hypernetMusic.description:
[Battle music] is chosen in Options. [Random] draws a different track at the start of every fight, [None] fights in silence.

[Map music] is seeded: one track per combination of biome, nation and time of day. Some music is generated live by a [procedural] system.

Whatever plays announces itself, as a notification or as a drawn cassette, with track and artist.

[Footsteps] change with the surface underfoot.

gamesOverview.title: Diversions
gamesOverview.description:
Most games are played [where you stand]: the pool table, the basketball court, the bowling alley and the chess board are set up on the map you are on.

Playing anything feeds the whole party's [Fun].

[2 players] can share almost all of them. Real time games let either player steer, turn based games become [hot seat].

gamesArcade.title: The Arcade Cabinet
gamesArcade.description:
Arcade cabinets take [tokens]. A cabinet keeps [high scores] with letter entry.

Each cart is a complete game:

- [Snake], against a computer snake competing for the same apples
- [Manpac], a pellet maze with 3 hunters and power pills that make them edible
- [Hoppa], across roads and rivers to 5 home slots
- [Astro Intruders], with destructible barriers
- [Meteoroids], with splitting rocks and a wrapping screen
- [Wallbreaker], with falling capsules
- [Crawler], splitting when shot in the middle, with a spider that eats the mushrooms
- [Bubble Pop], colours that stick and clusters that fall

gamesBowling.title: Bowling
gamesBowling.description:
Ten pin bowling at real dimensions: [18.29 m] to the head pin, a [1.07 m] lane, a [6.35 kg] ball and [1.53 kg] pins. The pins fall on their own weight, so a thin hit leaves a split.

[Aim], [power] and [spin] use the oscillating slider shared with pool and basketball.

gamesPool.title: Pool
gamesPool.description:
A [9 foot] table. Balls slow under cloth friction, throw each other off on impact, and rattle in the jaws of a pocket.

[Aim], [power] and [spin] use the oscillating slider.

gamesBasketball.title: Basketball
gamesBasketball.description:
A free throw shootout against a computer opponent: a [4.57 m] line and a rim [3.05 m] up.

The ball can bank off the backboard or rattle out of the rim.

gamesChess.title: Chess
gamesChess.description:
Full rules chess. Every piece is a creature, dealt from the [world seed], so one world always fields the same two armies.

[2 modes]: normal chess and [Chaos].

gamesFishing.title: Fishing
gamesFishing.description:
Cast into any fishable water. What takes the line is a fish, a piece of junk, or something hostile that you then have to fight.

Aim by looking around. A [ring] on the water shows where the cast lands.

gamesSurfing.title: Surfing
gamesSurfing.description:
Waves break along the beach rather than all at once, so the break travels sideways at about [10 m/s].

Stay ahead of the break to keep scoring. Fall behind it and the ride ends.

gamesShooting.title: The Shooting Range
gamesShooting.description:
A target range for [bows], [projectile weapons] and [firearms]. Each one handles exactly as it does in a fight.

The range [lends] you the weapon and takes it back at the door, so a weapon can be tried before it is bought.

gamesHorseRace.title: The Horse Race
gamesHorseRace.description:
Bet on a race, then watch it run.

Every runner is built from its own [name], so a named horse has the same form in every world.

[Odds] are computed by running the race many times in advance, so a short price is a real favourite.

gamesTournament.title: The Monster Tournament
gamesTournament.description:
A single elimination monster tournament to bet on. Pick a fighter, place a bet in [tokens], and only the fights involving your monster are shown.

The fights are fought for real: skills, costs, hit and crit rolls, states and poison all apply.

[Betting does not affect the outcome].

gamesGambling.title: Slots, Scratch Cards and Tarot
gamesGambling.description:
[Slot machine]: three reels for a stake in tokens, paying on matching symbols.

[Scratch cards]: a printed ticket, rubbed panel by panel in any order.

[Tarot table]: a reading, cut and turned one card at a time.

gamesPiano.title: The Piano
gamesPiano.description:
A playable [3 octave] keyboard, [C3 to B5]. The typing keyboard is laid out as two manuals, whites on one row and blacks above. A gamepad and the mouse also work.

Playing it feeds the [Fun] need.

gamesLockpick.title: Lockpicking
gamesLockpick.description:
Picking a lock is a [falling block puzzle]: a key bit must fit into a partly packed keyway, and the lock's [difficulty] sets how hard the fit is.

Failure consumes a [lockpick]. A [skeleton key] skips the game.

Lockpicking opens [locked doors] and [parked cars]. Being caught at it is a [crime].

gamesHyperTamer.title: HyperTamer
gamesHyperTamer.description:
A virtual pet with a [personality] that changes how it behaves.

It runs on [real time]: it eats, sleeps, plays and can [die of neglect], and time passes while the game is closed. Training minigames raise its stats.

gamesCards.title: The Card Game
gamesCards.description:
A collectible card game with a [collection], a [deck builder] and [duels].

A card is a monster, a weapon or a piece of armour from the game's database, printed with [5 stats] (STR, WIS, DEX, PSI, CON), each from [0 to 13]. Those numbers are [percentiles] against that card's own roster, not raw parameters. Equipment is bolted onto a monster already on the board and its values are added, clamped to [13].

A deck is [9 to 20 cards] and may only hold copies you own. A player who never opens the deck builder is dealt the best legal deck their collection allows.

A duel is [3x3]. On your turn you either [draw 3 cards] or [place one]: a monster onto a free tile, or gear onto one of your own monsters, [1 weapon] and [1 armour] each.

When the last tile is taken, every monster looks at its [4 orthogonal neighbours], picks the weakest enemy among them and fights it. Every pairing is scored against [one frozen snapshot] of the board and all deaths land together. [Most stats won] takes the fight, an equal count destroys both. Whoever has more monsters standing wins, ties broken on the summed stats of the survivors.

[Booster packs] hold [6 cards] from one pool, weighted so the last is never common.

Cards are also won by [capturing] a creature in battle. Capture picks the weakest creature still standing, helped by the caster's [PSI] against its own, and is impossible against anything more than [10 levels] above your median. Success adds the card and kills the creature, so the spoils still drop.

gamesRaman.title: The Raman Scanner
gamesRaman.description: A scanner that analyses the object you are facing: statues, paintings, masks, bookcases and library objects. It names the [material] and pays [knowledge points].

gamesPeriodic.title: The Periodic Table
gamesPeriodic.description: The periodic table, including lanthanides, actinides and a set of [esoteric elements] that appear in no real table. Selecting an element shows what it is and what it is used for.

arcaneSurge.description:
Raises [INT] by [50%]. Raises [WIS] by [50%]. Drains [10%] of max [MP] every turn.

Lasts [3-5 actions].
